title: 2024 National Licensure Examination: Comprehensive Clinical Nursing (Paper 1 - Acute Care & Med-Surg)
description: Complete high-yield clinical board examination covering patient prioritization, post-operative complications, cardiac arrhythmias, emergency drug titrations, and legal delegation.

questions.questionText: A registered nurse receives handoff on four clients. Which client requires immediate assessment FIRST?
options: A. A 58-year-old client with COPD with an oxygen saturation of 90% on 2 L/min nasal cannula.
B. A 64-year-old client 2 hours post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) who reports a hard, warm bulge at the femoral insertion site.
C. A 42-year-old client with type 1 diabetes whose morning blood glucose is 186 mg/dL prior to breakfast.
D. A 75-year-old client with chronic osteoarthritis reporting pain rated 7/10 requesting scheduled PRN acetaminophen.
questions.markingScheme: Award 5 marks for Option B. Option B indicates an active femoral arterial hematoma or pseudoaneurysm post-cardiac catheterization, risking massive retroperitoneal hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock.
questions.clinicalRationale: Airway, Breathing, Circulation (ABC) and acute vs chronic stability guidelines dictate that an expanding femoral bulge indicates active arterial bleeding. 90% SpO2 is expected in chronic COPD. Mild hyperglycemia and chronic joint pain are stable non-emergent concerns.
questions.highYieldTip: Rule of Prioritization: Always prioritize acute circulatory collapse or hemorrhage over chronic disease baselines.

questions.questionText: A client with heart failure is receiving intravenous furosemide 40 mg twice daily. The nurse notes new onset palpitations and muscle cramps. Which electrolyte imbalance and ECG alteration is most likely present?
options: B. Hypokalemia; prominent U waves and flattened T waves
C. Hyperkalemia; tall, peaked T waves and widened QRS
questions.markingScheme: Award 5 marks for Option B. Loop diuretics cause potassium wasting in the ascending limb of the loop of Henle, leading to hypokalemia, muscle cramping, ventricular irritability, and U waves.
questions.clinicalRationale: Furosemide is a potent loop diuretic that blocks Na-K-2Cl cotransporters. Serum potassium drops (< 3.5 mEq/L), manifesting with generalized muscle weakness, cramps, decreased bowel motility, flattened T waves, and distinctive U waves on ECG.
questions.highYieldTip: Remember: Hypokalemia = U waves and cramps; Hyperkalemia = Peaked T waves and widened QRS.

questions.questionText:
Clinical Vignette: A 28-year-old client G1P0 at 38 weeks gestation is admitted to the labor unit. Fetal heart rate monitoring demonstrates repetitive late decelerations following uterine contractions. The maternal BP is 98/60 mmHg following epidural placement.

Outline the four prioritized nursing actions (Intrauterine Resuscitation) the nurse must immediately institute.
questions.markingScheme:
Award 2.5 marks for each valid immediate intervention (total 10):
1. Reposition client onto left lateral side (relieves aortocaval compression and improves uteroplacental perfusion).
2. Administer high-flow supplemental oxygen via non-rebreather mask at 10 L/min.
3. Bolus intravenous fluids (isotonic crystalloids / Lactated Ringer’s) to correct maternal hypotension.
4. Discontinue / turn off oxytocin (Pitocin) infusion immediately if infusing, and notify the obstetric provider.
questions.clinicalRationale: Late decelerations indicate uteroplacental insufficiency. Epidural sympathetic blockade frequently precipitates maternal hypotension, decreasing placental blood flow. Immediate left tilt, oxygen, fluid expansion, and cessation of uterotonics are standard critical care resuscitation protocols.
questions.highYieldTip: Mnemonic for Intrauterine Resuscitation: "POISON" = Position change, Oxytocin off, IV fluid bolus, Sterile vaginal exam, Oxygen on, Notify MD.

questions.questionText:
A physician orders a continuous intravenous infusion of regular insulin at 0.1 units/kg/hour for a client in Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) weighing 70 kg. The pharmacy delivers a 250 mL normal saline bag containing 100 units of regular insulin.

Calculate the required IV pump infusion rate in mL/hour.
questions.markingScheme:
Award 5 marks for 17.5 mL/hr (or 18 mL/hr if rounding policy allows):
Step 1: Desired dose = 70 kg * 0.1 units/kg/hr = 7 units/hr.
Step 2: Concentration = 100 units / 250 mL = 0.4 units/mL.
Step 3: Pump rate = 7 units/hr / 0.4 units/mL = 17.5 mL/hr.
questions.clinicalRationale: Accurate weight-based dose calculation is essential in DKA to avoid rapid hypoglycemia and cerebral edema.
questions.highYieldTip: Always double-check units/kg/hr vs total units/hr!

title: 2023 Midterm Assessment: Pharmacology & Safe Drug Calculations (Paper 2)
authorOrInstitution: School of Nursing & Midwifery Examination Board
description: High-alert medication calculations, therapeutic serum levels, antidote associations, and autonomic receptor pharmacology past paper with complete worked answers.

questions.questionText: A client prescribed digoxin 0.25 mg daily reports visual changes describing halos around street lights, accompanied by nausea and fatigue. What is the immediate nursing priority?
options: A. Administer the scheduled dose with an antacid to relieve nausea.
B. Hold the dose, evaluate apical pulse, and request serum digoxin and potassium levels.
C. Instruct the client to visit an ophthalmologist for corrective lenses.
D. Encourage increased dietary intake of potassium and recheck in 48 hours.
questions.markingScheme: Award 5 marks for Option B. Halos around lights, nausea, and bradycardia are classic cardinal symptoms of digitalis toxicity. Normal therapeutic range is 0.5 - 2.0 ng/mL. Hypokalemia increases susceptibility to toxicity.
questions.clinicalRationale: Holding the medication and assessing apical heart rate prevents fatal ventricular arrhythmias. Therapeutic serum blood levels and electrolytes must be confirmed.

questions.questionText: Which medication is the designated specific reversal agent for severe heparin-induced bleeding?
questions.markingScheme: Award 5 marks for Option B. Protamine sulfate is a strongly basic protein that binds to strongly acidic heparin to form a stable, inactive salt complex.
questions.clinicalRationale: Protamine sulfate neutralizes unfractionated heparin within 5 minutes of intravenous delivery. Vitamin K is for warfarin reversal. Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines.
questions.highYieldTip: Antidote Pairs: Heparin -> Protamine Sulfate; Warfarin -> Vitamin K.

title: 2023 Semester Final: Maternal, Neonatal & Pediatric Nursing Practice (Paper 3)
description: Pediatric dehydration assessment, congenital heart defects (cyanotic vs acyanotic), APGAR scoring scenarios, and pediatric medication safety.

questions.questionText:
A newborn infant is assessed at 1 minute of life: Heart rate is 110 bpm, respiratory effort is vigorous with lusty crying, active motion and flexion of extremities, prompt grimacing and coughing to suction catheter, and body is pink with mild cyanosis of the hands and feet (acrocyanosis).

Calculate the 1-minute APGAR score and provide the breakdown for each of the 5 criteria.
questions.markingScheme:
Award 10 marks total (2 marks per criteria):
- Appearance (Color): 1 (pink body, blue extremities / acrocyanosis)
- Pulse (Heart Rate): 2 (> 100 bpm)
- Grimace (Reflex Irritability): 2 (vigorous cry/cough to suction)
- Activity (Muscle Tone): 2 (active flexion and motion)
- Respiration: 2 (strong, vigorous cry)
TOTAL APGAR SCORE: 9 / 10. Indicates excellent neonatal transition.
questions.clinicalRationale: Acrocyanosis is physiological and normal in the first 24-48 hours of life, docking only 1 point under Appearance.
questions.highYieldTip: APGAR is scored at 1 and 5 minutes (and 10 mins if score < 7).

title: High-Yield Clinical Lab Values & Critical Interpretation Cheat Sheet
description: Essential reference sheet containing standard normal ranges, critical panic levels, clinical signs of derangement, and emergency nursing priorities for adult inpatients.
highYieldKeyPoints: Potassium (3.5 - 5.0 mEq/L): Most critical cardiac electrolyte. Never infuse IV push.
Sodium (135 - 145 mEq/L): Neurological manifestations (seizure precautions in severe hyponatremia < 120).
Normal ABG Values: pH 7.35-7.45 | PaCO2 35-45 mmHg | HCO3 22-26 mEq/L | PaO2 80-100 mmHg.
INR: Normal 0.8 - 1.2 | Therapeutic Warfarin 2.0 - 3.0 | Mechanical Heart Valve 2.5 - 3.5.

sections.title: 1. Core Serum Electrolytes & Critical Interventions
sections.content: Electrolyte disturbances alter neuromuscular transmission, cardiac conduction, and cellular volume equilibrium.
bulletPoints: Sodium (Na+): 135 - 145 mEq/L. Hyponatremia (<135) causes cerebral edema, confusion, seizures. Rapid correction risks osmotic demyelination syndrome.
Potassium (K+): 3.5 - 5.0 mEq/L. Hypokalemia (<3.5): flattened T, U waves, PVCs, muscle weakness. Hyperkalemia (>5.0): peaked T waves, widened QRS, asystole risk.
Total Calcium (Ca2+): 8.5 - 10.5 mg/dL. Hypocalcemia signs: Positive Chvostek’s (facial twitching) and Trousseau’s (carpal spasm with BP cuff).
Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5 - 2.5 mEq/L. Low magnesium predisposes to Torsades de Pointes. Hypermagnesemia depresses deep tendon reflexes.

callout.text: EMERGENCY RULE: Intravenous Potassium Chloride (KCl) must NEVER be administered via IV Push or Bolus! Max peripheral infusion concentration is 10 mEq/hour to prevent fatal cardiac arrest.

sections.title: 2. Complete Blood Count (CBC) Ranges
sections.content: Baseline hematologic parameters for infection, anemia, and bleeding risks.
bulletPoints: White Blood Cells (WBC): 4,500 - 11,000 /mcL (Leukocytosis > 11k suggests infection; Neutropenia < 1,500 demands neutropenic precautions).
Hemoglobin (Hgb): Males: 13.8 - 17.2 g/dL | Females: 12.1 - 15.1 g/dL. Transfusion trigger commonly < 7.0 g/dL in non-cardiac patients.
Hematocrit (Hct): Males: 40% - 50% | Females: 36% - 48% (Hct is roughly 3x Hemoglobin).
Platelets (Plt): 150,000 - 450,000 /mcL (<50,000 triggers bleeding precautions; <20,000 risk of spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage).

sections.title: 3. Arterial Blood Gas (ABG) Analysis - ROME Framework
sections.content: Use the ROME mnemonic (Respiratory Opposite, Metabolic Equal) to interpret arterial balance:
bulletPoints: Step 1: Check pH (Normal: 7.35 - 7.45). < 7.35 = Acidosis | > 7.45 = Alkalosis.
Step 2: Check PaCO2 (Respiratory, Normal: 35 - 45 mmHg). If pH is LOW and PaCO2 is HIGH -> Respiratory Acidosis.
Step 3: Check HCO3 (Metabolic, Normal: 22 - 26 mEq/L). If pH is LOW and HCO3 is LOW -> Metabolic Acidosis.
Compensation: If pH is abnormal and the opposing system is altering to compensate, it is Partially Compensated. If pH has returned to normal range, it is Fully Compensated.

title: Standardized Nursing Care Plan: Acute Coronary Syndrome & Myocardial Infarction
description: Evidence-based NANDA-I nursing care plan outlining priority diagnoses, targeted interventions with physiological rationales, and evaluation criteria for acute myocardial infarction.
highYieldKeyPoints: Priority 1: Acute Pain related to myocardial tissue ischemia secondary to reduced coronary artery perfusion.
Priority 2: Ineffective Tissue Perfusion (Cardiopulmonary) related to thrombus formation.
MONA Protocol: Morphine, Oxygen, Nitroglycerin, Aspirin (Chewable 325 mg).
Door-to-balloon time goal for primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) is < 90 minutes.

sections.title: Nursing Diagnosis 1: Acute Pain (Chest / Anginal)
sections.content: Related to myocardial ischemia and accumulation of lactic acid metabolites as evidenced by verbalization of crushing substernal chest pressure radiating to left arm/jaw, diaphoresis, and facial grimacing.
bulletPoints: Intervention 1: Immediately place client on strict bed rest in Semi-Fowler’s position. (Rationale: Reduces venous return to the heart, lowers myocardial workload and oxygen consumption).
Intervention 2: Administer supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula if SpO2 < 90%. (Rationale: Enhances myocardial arterial oxygen delivery to ischemic border zones).

Intervention 3: Administer Sublingual Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg every 5 minutes up to 3 doses as prescribed, verifying systolic BP > 90 mmHg prior to each dose. (Rationale: Promotes peripheral and coronary vasodilation, reducing preload and afterload).
Intervention 4: Administer IV Morphine Sulfate 2-4 mg as titrated. (Rationale: Relieves ischemic chest pain, reduces anxiety, and causes mild venodilation lowering cardiac preload).

callout.text: Contraindication: Never administer Nitroglycerin if the patient has ingested phosphodiesterase inhibitors (e.g. Sildenafil) within 24-48 hours due to risk of refractory lethal hypotension.

sections.title: Nursing Diagnosis 2: Risk for Decreased Cardiac Output
sections.content: Related to altered myocardial contractility, changes in heart rate and electrical conduction as evidenced by dysrhythmias and decreased blood pressure.
bulletPoints: Intervention: Maintain continuous 12-lead ECG telemetry monitoring. (Rationale: Ventricular fibrillation is the leading cause of early death in acute STEMI).
Intervention: Monitor hourly intake and urinary output, reporting < 30 mL/hr. (Rationale: Decreased renal perfusion is an early sensitive indicator of failing cardiac output).
Intervention: Have emergency resuscitation defibrillator and crash cart at bedside ready for immediate countershock.

title: Pediatric & Adult Drug Calculation Formula Master Guide
description: Formulas for oral solids, liquid volumes, IV infusion pump rates (mL/hr), manual gravity drip factor calculations (gtt/min), and continuous microgram/kg/min infusions.
highYieldKeyPoints: Basic Formula: (Desired / Have) * Volume = Dosage Amount to Administer.
Manual IV Drop Rate: (Total Volume in mL * Drop Factor gtt/mL) / Time in Minutes = Drops per minute (gtt/min).
Infusion Pump Rate: Total Volume (mL) / Time (hours) = mL/hour.
Microgram/kg/minute: Rate (mL/hr) = (Dose mcg/kg/min * Weight kg * 60 min/hr) / Concentration in mcg/mL.

sections.title: Essential Formulas & Worked Examples
sections.content: Step-by-step methods for clinical calculations without rounding errors:
bulletPoints: 1. Oral Tablet Formula: Dose Desired / Dose on Hand = Number of tablets. (Example: Order: Metoprolol 50 mg PO. On hand: 25 mg tablets. Calculation: 50 / 25 = 2 tablets).
2. Liquid Dosage: (Desired / Have) * Quantity. (Example: Order: Amoxicillin 250 mg. On hand: 125 mg / 5 mL. Calculation: (250 / 125) * 5 = 10 mL).

3. Gravity IV Drip: Volume (mL) * Drop Factor (gtt/mL) / Duration (minutes). (Example: Infuse 1000 mL NS over 8 hours using 15 gtt/mL tubing. 8 hours = 480 mins. (1000 * 15) / 480 = 31.25 -> 31 gtt/min).

title: Cranial Nerves (I - XII) Assessment & Neurological Mnemonics
description: Comprehensive cranial nerve examination guide with sensory/motor functions, assessment techniques, pathological signs, and standard mnemonics.
highYieldKeyPoints: Name Mnemonic: "On Old Olympus’ Towering Tops, A Finn And German Viewed Some Hops"
Function Mnemonic (Sensory, Motor, Both): "Some Say Marry Money, But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter More"
CN III, IV, VI tested together via 6 cardinal fields of gaze.
CN X (Vagus): Assessed via uvula symmetry on saying "Ah" and gag reflex.

sections.title: Cranial Nerve Breakdown Table
sections.content: Summary of clinical testing methodology for bed-side assessment:
bulletPoints: CN I (Olfactory - Sensory): Smell identification with eyes closed.
CN II (Optic - Sensory): Snellen visual acuity chart and visual confrontation fields.
CN III, IV, VI (Oculomotor, Trochlear, Abducens - Motor): EOMs, pupillary light reflex (PERRLA), accommodation.
CN V (Trigeminal - Both): Light touch across 3 facial branches; clench jaw / masseter muscle tone.
CN VII (Facial - Both): Smile, frown, puff cheeks, raise eyebrows symmetrically.
CN VIII (Vestibulocochlear - Sensory): Whisper voice test; Weber and Rinne tuning fork tests.
CN IX & X (Glossopharyngeal & Vagus - Both): Symmetrical uvula rise; swallowing and speech quality.
CN XI (Spinal Accessory - Motor): Shoulder shrug against resistance; head turn against resistance.
CN XII (Hypoglossal - Motor): Tongue protrusion in midline; assess for fasciculations or deviation.

title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: Clinical Practice Guidelines & Hour-1 Resuscitation Bundle
authorOrInstitution: International Sepsis Guidelines Committee & Acute Care Nursing Council
description: Evidence-based acute resuscitation protocol for bedside nurses, detailing immediate lactate measurement, blood culture timing, broad-spectrum antimicrobial administration, 30 mL/kg crystalloid fluid resuscitation, and vasopressor titration.
highYieldKeyPoints: Time Zero: Defined as triage presentation or clinical deterioration onset.
Measure Serum Lactate immediately; repeat within 2-4 hours if initial > 2.0 mmol/L.
Obtain blood cultures (2 sets from distinct venipuncture sites) PRIOR to antibiotic administration without causing substantial delay (>45 min).
Administer broad-spectrum IV antimicrobials within 1 hour of recognition.
Begin rapid administration of 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloids for hypotension or lactate ≥ 4.0 mmol/L.
First-line vasopressor of choice is Norepinephrine (titrate for MAP ≥ 65 mmHg).
documentContentText:
SURVIVING SEPSIS CAMPAIGN: CLINICAL PRACTICE PROTOCOL
REVISION: 2024 INTERNATIONAL CONSENSUS

1. CLINICAL CRITERIA & RECOGNITION (SOFA & qSOFA)
Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection.
qSOFA (Quick Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment) Bedside Screening (≥2 flags risk):
  - Respiratory Rate ≥ 22 breaths/min
  - Altered Mental Status (GCS < 15)
  - Systolic Blood Pressure ≤ 100 mmHg

2. THE HOUR-1 RESUSCITATION BUNDLE (ALL TO BE INITIATED WITHIN 60 MINUTES OF TIME ZERO)
Element 1: Measure Blood Lactate Concentration
  - Initial lactate > 2 mmol/L reflects cellular hypoperfusion.
  - Lactate ≥ 4 mmol/L indicates severe tissue dysoxia; requires immediate mandatory 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus.
  - Repeat lactate within 2 to 4 hours to verify clearance (therapeutic goal: ≥10-20% reduction every 2 hours).

Element 2: Obtain Blood Cultures Prior to Antibiotics
  - Draw two sets of blood cultures (one aerobic, one anaerobic per venipuncture site).
  - Do NOT delay antibiotic start by more than 45 minutes if blood culture procurement is prolonged.

Element 3: Administer Broad-Spectrum IV Antimicrobials
  - Initiate empiric broad-spectrum coverage tailored to suspected source (e.g., respiratory, urinary, intra-abdominal, central line).
  - Infuse maximum recommended loading doses to achieve rapid therapeutic serum concentrations.

Element 4: Rapid Administration of 30 mL/kg Intravenous Crystalloid
  - Indicated for SBP < 90 mmHg, MAP < 65 mmHg, or serum lactate ≥ 4.0 mmol/L.
  - Use balanced crystalloids (e.g., Lactated Ringer's or Plasma-Lyte) in preference to 0.9% Normal Saline to mitigate hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.
  - Infuse via wide-bore peripheral lines (18G or 16G) or central venous catheter.

Element 5: Apply Vasopressors for Refractory Hypotension
  - If MAP remains < 65 mmHg despite or during fluid administration, initiate vasopressors immediately.
  - Norepinephrine (Levophed) is the first-line vasopressor (start at 2-5 mcg/min and titrate rapidly).
  - Target: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) ≥ 65 mmHg.
  - Vasopressin (0.03 units/min fixed infusion) may be added to reduce Norepinephrine requirements.

3. NURSING MONITORING & SAFETY CHECKLIST
  - Continuous ECG and non-invasive blood pressure monitoring every 5-15 minutes until stabilized.
  - Strict hourly urine output measurement via Foley catheter with urometer (Target > 0.5 mL/kg/hour).
  - Frequent dynamic assessment of fluid responsiveness (passive leg raise test, pulse pressure variation).
  - Escalate to Critical Care / Medical Emergency Team (MET) immediately if refractory to Hour-1 bundle.

title: Standard Operating Procedure: Safe Intravenous Medication Administration & High-Alert Verification
authorOrInstitution: Hospital Pharmacy & Clinical Nursing Safety Board
description: Definitive clinical procedure for intravenous medication administration, including independent double-checking of high-alert medications (Insulin, Heparin, Potassium, Opioids), smart infusion pump programming, and extravasation prevention.
highYieldKeyPoints: The Eight Rights of Medication: Patient, Drug, Dose, Route, Time, Documentation, Reason, Response.
Independent Double-Check: Two registered nurses must independently verify calculation, vial, dilution, and pump programming for high-alert drugs.
High-Alert PINCH Drugs: Potassium, Insulin, Narcotics/Opioids, Chemotherapy, Heparin/Anticoagulants.
Never administer IV Potassium Chloride as an undiluted IV push (causes fatal cardiac arrest).
Assess peripheral IV site for patency, blood return, and absence of swelling/erythema prior to any IV push or infusion.
documentContentText:
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE: INTRAVENOUS MEDICATION ADMINISTRATION
SAFETY CODE: SOP-MED-044-REV3

1. PURPOSE & PRINCIPLES
To standardize the safe preparation, reconstitution, rate calculation, verification, and administration of intravenous medications to prevent preventable adverse drug events.

2. INDEPENDENT DOUBLE-CHECK PROTOCOL (HIGH-ALERT MEDICATIONS)
High-Alert Drugs (Acronym PINCH):
  P - Potassium & Concentrated Electrolytes
  I - Insulin (all subcutaneous and IV infusions)
  N - Narcotics / Opioids (continuous infusions, PCA pumps)
  C - Chemotherapeutic Agents
  H - Heparin & Direct Thrombin Inhibitors

Verification Procedure:
  1. Nurse 1 reviews the physician order in EHR, selects the drug vial, checks expiration date, and performs dosage calculation.
  2. Nurse 2 independently inspects the order, recalculates the dose without prompting, and cross-checks the syringe volume or infusion concentration.
  3. Both nurses jointly verify the patient identity at bedside using two unique identifiers (Full Name, Medical Record Number, Date of Birth).
  4. Both nurses verify the smart pump channel and drug library limits prior to pressing "START".

3. IV SITE ASSESSMENT & COMPATIBILITY
  - Check IV cannula site: Inspect for warmth, swelling, pallor, or tenderness.
  - Flush with 3-5 mL of sterile 0.9% Normal Saline before and after medication to confirm patency and clear incompatible residuals.
  - Consult IV compatibility matrix (Trissel's) before "piggybacking" medications into maintenance IV fluids.

4. INFUSION PUMP RATE FORMULA REFERENCE
Flow Rate (mL/hr) = Total Volume (mL) ÷ Total Time (hours)
Drip Rate (gtt/min) = [Total Volume (mL) × Drop Factor (gtt/mL)] ÷ Time in Minutes
Dosage Rate (mcg/kg/min) = [Pump Rate (mL/hr) × Concentration (mcg/mL)] ÷ [Weight (kg) × 60]

5. EXTRAVASATION MANAGEMENT
If extravasation of vesicant (e.g., Dopamine, Norepinephrine, Chemotherapy, Calcium Chloride) is suspected:
  - STOP the infusion immediately.
  - Aspirate residual drug from the catheter with a 3 mL syringe.
  - Do NOT flush the line. Remove cannula carefully.
  - Elevate affected extremity above heart level.
  - Apply warm or cold compress as specific antidote protocol dictates (e.g., Phentolamine for vasopressor extravasation).

title: Clinical Protocol: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) & STEMI Rapid Assessment Algorithm
description: Standardized guideline for triage, 12-lead ECG acquisition within 10 minutes, high-sensitivity troponin serial testing, MONA-B initial medical management, and primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) preparation.
highYieldKeyPoints: Door-to-ECG Time: Obtain and interpret 12-Lead ECG within 10 minutes of patient arrival with chest discomfort.
Door-to-Balloon Time (PCI): Target ≤ 90 minutes from first medical contact to device activation in catheterization laboratory.
STEMI Criteria: ST-segment elevation ≥ 1 mm (0.1 mV) in ≥ 2 contiguous limb leads or ≥ 2 mm in precordial leads V2-V3.
Nitroglycerin Contraindication: Never administer Nitroglycerin if SBP < 90 mmHg, HR < 50 bpm, suspected right ventricular infarct, or recent phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor use.
Administer Aspirin 162-325 mg chewed immediately for non-enteric coated rapid platelet inhibition.
documentContentText:
CLINICAL PROTOCOL: ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROME (ACS)
INSTITUTIONAL CLINICAL STANDARD

1. TRIAGE & IMMEDIATE BEDSIDE ASSESSMENT (WITHIN 10 MINUTES)
Every patient presenting with non-traumatic chest pain, pressure, epigastric discomfort, radiating jaw/arm pain, or unexplained acute dyspnea must be triaged immediately as High Acuity.
  - Step 1: Immediate bed placement with cardiac monitor and continuous pulse oximetry.
  - Step 2: Obtain 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. Transmit to emergency physician or cardiologist immediately.
  - Step 3: Establish large-bore IV access (18G or 20G).
  - Step 4: Draw baseline cardiac biomarkers (high-sensitivity cardiac Troponin I/T), CBC, electrolytes, coagulation profile.

2. INITIAL MEDICAL THERAPY (MONA-B GUIDELINE)
  - Oxygen: Administer supplemental O2 ONLY if SpO2 < 90% or patient in respiratory distress (hyperoxia causes coronary vasoconstriction).
  - Aspirin: 162 mg to 325 mg non-enteric coated, chewed immediately for rapid buccal absorption.
  - Nitroglycerin: Sublingual 0.4 mg tablet or spray every 5 minutes (maximum 3 doses). Assess BP before each dose.
      * CONTRAINDICATIONS: SBP < 90 mmHg, heart rate < 50 or > 100 bpm, right ventricular infarction (Leads V3R, V4R ST elevation), or PDE-5 inhibitor use within 24-48 hours.
  - Morphine Sulfate: 2 to 4 mg IV push for severe ischemic pain refractory to nitrates (use judiciously due to potential delay in antiplatelet absorption).
  - Beta-Blocker: Oral Metoprolol tartrate 25-50 mg within 24 hours if no signs of heart failure, low cardiac output, or cardiogenic shock risk.

3. REPERFUSION STRATEGY (STEMI)
  - Primary PCI: Preferred reperfusion modality. Door-to-balloon time goal ≤ 90 minutes.
  - Fibrinolytic Therapy: Indicated ONLY if anticipated transfer to PCI-capable facility exceeds 120 minutes. Door-to-needle time goal ≤ 30 minutes (e.g., Tenecteplase, Alteplase). Check absolute contraindications for intracranial hemorrhage risk.

4. POST-PROCEDURAL NURSING CARE (FEMORAL OR RADIAL SHEATH)
  - Radial Artery Band (TR Band): Monitor pulse, capillary refill, warmth, and radial pressure. Wean pressure per titration protocol.
  - Femoral Access: Strict flat bed rest for 4-6 hours if manual compression used; monitor pedal pulses and groin puncture site for hematoma or pseudoaneurysm.

title: Obstetric Emergency Protocol: Active Management of Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)
description: Stage-based clinical response to postpartum hemorrhage, quantitative blood loss (QBL) measurement, bimanual uterine compression, and stepwise uterotonic drug administration (Oxytocin, Methylergonovine, Carboprost, Misoprostol).
highYieldKeyPoints: PPH Definition: Cumulative blood loss ≥ 1,000 mL or blood loss accompanied by signs/symptoms of hypovolemia within 24 hours post-birth.
Quantitative Blood Loss (QBL): Mandatory gravimetric weighing of sponges and calibrated collection drapes (visual estimation underestimates loss by 50%).
The 4 Ts of PPH Etiology: Tone (70%, uterine atony), Trauma (20%), Tissue (10%, retained placenta), Thrombin (1%, coagulopathy).
Uterine Fundal Massage: Immediate primary nursing intervention for uterine atony (boggy uterus).
Carboprost Tromethamine (Hemabate) Contraindication: Severe asthma or reactive airway disease (triggers bronchospasm).
Methylergonovine (Methergine) Contraindication: Hypertension or preeclampsia (causes severe peripheral vasoconstriction).
documentContentText:
OBSTETRIC EMERGENCY GUIDELINE: POSTPARTUM HEMORRHAGE (PPH)
STANDARDS OF CARE & STEPWISE PROTOCOL

1. IMMEDIATE ASSESSMENT & STAGE IDENTIFICATION
Measure Quantitative Blood Loss (QBL) from delivery: 1 gram of weight increase = 1 mL of blood loss.
  - Stage 1: Blood loss > 500 mL (vaginal) or > 1000 mL (cesarean) with normal vital signs.
  - Stage 2: Continued bleeding (loss 1000 - 1500 mL) OR abnormal vitals (HR > 110, BP < 85/45).
  - Stage 3: Blood loss > 1500 mL, continued hemorrhage, or clinical shock. Activate Massive Transfusion Protocol (MTP).

2. FIRST-LINE NURSING ACTIONS (STAGE 1 - AT BEDPOST)
  - Vigorously massage the uterine fundus to expel clots and stimulate myometrial contractions.
  - Empty the urinary bladder via straight catheter (distended bladder displaces uterus and prevents contraction).
  - Ensure dual wide-bore IV access (18G or 16G).
  - Administer high-flow supplemental oxygen (10 L/min via non-rebreather mask).

3. STEPWISE UTEROTONIC DRUG ALGORITHM
Order of Administration:
  1. Oxytocin (Pitocin):
     - Dose: 20 to 40 units in 1,000 mL crystalloid infused at 500 mL/hr, OR 10 units IM.
     - Note: First-line for all deliveries. Never administer undiluted rapid IV push (causes severe hypotension and arrhythmias).
  2. Methylergonovine (Methergine):
     - Dose: 0.2 mg IM every 2-4 hours (maximum 5 doses).
     - CONTRAINDICATION: Pre-existing hypertension, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or coronary disease.
  3. Carboprost Tromethamine (Hemabate):
     - Dose: 250 mcg (0.25 mg) deep IM every 15-90 minutes (maximum 8 doses).
     - CONTRAINDICATION: Active asthma or bronchospasm. Common side effects: profuse diarrhea, pyrexia.
  4. Misoprostol (Cytotec):
     - Dose: 800 to 1,000 mcg per rectum, or 600 mcg sublingually/orally.
     - Safe in hypertensive and asthmatic patients.

4. MECHANICAL & SURGICAL INTERVENTIONS (STAGE 2 - 3)
  - Perform bimanual uterine compression.
  - Intrauterine balloon tamponade (Bakri Balloon): Inflate with 300 - 500 mL sterile saline to tamponade placental bed.
  - Tranexamic Acid (TXA): 1 gram IV over 10 minutes, administered within 3 hours of birth.
  - Prepare patient for surgical intervention (B-Lynch suture, uterine artery embolization, or emergency hysterectomy).
